findings.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — `<%- end if %>` — stray trailing `if` on the block terminator. Adversarial verified the compiled ERB emits `; end if ; _erbout << ...` → Ruby syntax error, so **every request that finds an existing topic 500s**; the feature is dead on its only happy path. Correctness reads it as a parsed modifier that inverts header output order instead. Either way it is wrong and unrendered by any test.

app/models/post.rb:133` (+ `topic_embed.rb:22`, `poll_feed.rb:35`) — `cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `cook_method == :raw_html`, and `TopicEmbed.import` feeds it externally-sourced HTML with **no sanitization**. The RSS path actively worsens it: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` converts entity-escaped feed markup back into live markup before storing. Rendered unfiltered at `best.html.erb:19` (`raw post.cooked`) and everywhere else posts render. → stored XSS on the forum origin, including against admins.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — Throttle key is `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` — raw attacker-supplied URL, no canonicalization, no per-IP/host/global budget. `?x=1`, `#a`, trailing slash, case variants each get a distinct key *and* a distinct `TopicEmbed` row. N URL variants ⇒ N Sidekiq jobs ⇒ N outbound fetches ⇒ N duplicate topics authored as `embed_by_username`. Simultaneously a Sidekiq DoS, an outbound amplifier aimed at the publisher's own site, and a forum-flooding vector.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — The **entire** authorization on this endpoint is `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. `Referer` is a plain header — any non-browser client sets it and is fully authorized. `embed_url` is never validated in the controller at all before reaching `Jobs.enqueue`. This gate stops honest browsers and zero attackers; findings #3, #6, #7 all hang off it.

spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:33-41 — Silent-pass verification: every example stubs `perform_retrieve` and `retrieved_recently?` — **private methods of the object under test**. The whole body of `perform_retrieve` and the entire redis throttle could be deleted and all 5 specs stay green. The security-relevant core of the feature is verified only by mocks of itself.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` with no `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, no size cap, no redirect restriction, no rescue. open-uri follows redirects to *any* target, so a common open-redirect on the embeddable host (`/out?url=`) satisfies the host allowlist on the initial URL and lands the fetch on `127.0.0.1` / `169.254.169.254` — anonymous SSRF whose response body is then imported into a public topic. Also pins/OOMs a Sidekiq worker on a slow or multi-GB response. Same at `poll_feed.rb:29`.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs the *entire* RSS import synchronously inside the request-triggered job, once per cache-missing embed_url — converting an hourly job into an anonymous on-demand one, with nothing serializing concurrent copies. Feeds whose HTML shifts between fetches (ads, timestamps, nonces) re-revise and **bump every topic** on every forced poll (`bypass_bump` not passed) — a remote-controlled forum-spam button.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — `$redis.setnx` + separate `$redis.expire` is **not atomic**. A crash, failover, or connection drop between the two lines leaves a key with no TTL → that embed_url is throttled *forever*, unrecoverable without manual redis surgery, and the iframe loops on "Loading Discussion…" in perpetuity. Needs `SET k v EX 60 NX`. No rescue around `$redis` either, so a redis outage hard-fails every job.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — `if post.present?` can never be false — `PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even on failure (the failed save raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback`, swallowed by the *nested* `Topic.transaction` with no savepoint), leaving an unsaved post with `id == nil`. `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: nil, post_id: nil)` then violates the `null: false` columns, turning a recoverable rejection into `StatementInvalid` that kills the caller. Should check `post.persisted?`.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `url` interpolated raw into an HTML attribute: `"<a href='#{url}'>"`, guarded only by a `^https?://` prefix check. A feed `link`/`id` of `http://x/' onmouseover='…` breaks out of the attribute — and the result is stored as `raw_html` and never escaped. Fully attacker-controlled field.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — `request.referer` interpolated unescaped into a JS single-quoted string literal. ERB escaping produces HTML entities, not JS-string escaping, and `ensure_embeddable` constrains only the *host* — path/query are attacker-controlled and can contain `'` or `</script>`. Reflected XSS in a frame running on the forum origin. Passing a full URL as `targetOrigin` is also protocol-wrong (must be scheme://host[:port]).

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48-52 — Readability's `attributes: %w[href src]` whitelist preserves attribute *values* without any scheme validation. `javascript:` hrefs and `data:` / attacker-hosted `src` survive into a `raw_html` post. Readability is a content extractor, not a sanitizer.

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `force: true` added to an **already-shipped migration** — emits `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics` before create, destroying rows with no rollback path. Inert where the version is already in `schema_migrations`, so new installs and existing installs permanently diverge. Unrelated to this PR's stated intent. The fix for a bad released migration is a follow-up migration, never an in-place edit.

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` on the largest table in a Discourse install. On pre-PG11 this rewrites the whole table + every index under `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE`. No `disable_ddl_transaction!`, no lock_timeout, no add-nullable/backfill/set-NOT-NULL split — contrast `20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb`, which does exactly that for the same table. Full site outage during deploy on a large forum.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every embed_url miss unconditionally enqueues a job — no enqueue-time rate limit or dedupe — while `loading.html.erb:9` reloads every 30s. N concurrent viewers ⇒ N jobs immediately, 2N/min thereafter. The redis throttle suppresses the *work* inside the job but not the request/enqueue volume.

app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8 — Unbounded client reload loop: no attempt counter, no backoff, no terminal state. For any permanently-unresolvable URL (publisher 404, unset `embed_by_username`, stuck throttle key, deleted post) every visitor becomes a permanent 2-req/min bot; traffic scales with pageviews on a broken article and never self-terminates.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `i.content.scrub` assumes non-nil `content` — SimpleRSS returns nil for RSS 2.0 items carrying only `description`, and for Atom `summary`. `i.title` can likewise be nil into `PostCreator(skip_validations: true)` → `topics.title` NOT NULL violation. With `retry: false` the exception aborts the whole hourly poll: every item after the bad one is silently never imported, no error surfaced. Whole common feed formats fail on item one.

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:14,20,26,35 — `poll_feed` is mocked in all four examples — the entire body (user lookup, `SimpleRSS.parse`, the `url = i.id` fallback, `unescapeHTML`, `TopicEmbed.import`) has zero coverage. Delete the body and the spec passes. No RSS/Atom fixture anywhere in the diff.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:113-116,148 — Unrelated feature removal: `--category`/`-c` deleted with no deprecation (existing scripted invocations now abort on "Unknown switches"), and the `PostCreator` call replaced with `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, silently dropping the `created_at` backdating for every imported topic. Not mentioned in the PR intent, no test covers the task.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin comparison. `https://discuss.example.co` passes against `https://discuss.example.com`; conversely a correct origin fails whenever scheme normalization differs, silently killing resize. No check that the message came from `iframe.contentWindow`. This is the client-side mirror of finding #4 — both "validations" in this PR are string comparisons dressed as origin checks.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:15` & `:49 — Host-validation logic and the `embed_by_username` user lookup are each duplicated verbatim between `TopicRetriever` and (`embed_controller.rb:26` / `poll_feed.rb:25`). No shared helper. The next normalization fix (scheme, `www.`, port, case) lands in one copy → an endpoint that accepts a referer it will then refuse to retrieve for. Both user-lookup copies also `NoMethodError` on `nil.downcase`.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15` vs `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — The controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, …)` but its own spec asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)`. Nothing in the request path constructs `TopicRetriever` directly; the spec cannot pass under Sidekiq fake mode. The new public route's cold-start contract (sync vs. background) is contradicted by its own test.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:21-30 — `PostCreator#create` performs non-transactional side effects inside the wrapping `Topic.transaction`: `enqueue_jobs`, MessageBus `publish`, and the redis `store_unique_post_key`. On the `RecordNotUnique` race the DB rolls back but none of those do → orphaned jobs referencing a vanished `post_id`, and the surviving redis unique-key rejects the legitimate retry as a duplicate. Embed never appears; loading page loops forever.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — Also a P1 contract defect independent of the injection: `targetOrigin` receives a full URL rather than an origin, so a referer with a path breaks resize for every embedder.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — `revisor.revise!` return value discarded, yet `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, …)` runs unconditionally. `revise!` returns false without touching the post when `should_revise?` is false. The sha1 then claims sync that never happened, and since all future updates gate on `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, the post is **stuck at stale content forever**.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — `post = embed.post` used unguarded at `PostRevisor.new(post)`. No FK, no `dependent:`, nothing deletes `topic_embeds` rows when a post/topic is destroyed → dangling `post_id`, `embed.post` is nil, `should_revise?` calls `@post.raw` → NoMethodError. Permanently breaks that URL's import path and (per #17) the feed poll with it.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — `TopicView.new(topic_id, …)` with no rescue and no check that the topic still exists or is visible anonymously. Routine moderation (delete a topic) turns the publisher's embed into a permanent 500 — not a loading page, not an empty state — and `perform_retrieve` bails on the surviving `TopicEmbed` row, so there is no self-healing path.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-29 — Check-then-insert race against the new UNIQUE index: `where(embed_url:).first` … HTTP fetch … `create!`. PollFeed (hourly) and RetrieveTopic (per request) interleave, and `no_throttle` for staff removes the guard entirely. Loser hits the unique violation, aborting the transaction and killing the enclosing job; with `retry: false` the rest of that feed run is never processed.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — `params.require(:embed_url)` accepts arrays and hashes. `?embed_url[]=a&embed_url[]=b` enqueues an Array; `URI(array)` raises `TypeError`/`ArgumentError`, which the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` does **not** catch. Unbounded stream of hard-failing retrying jobs from any anonymous user. The defensive rescue reads as covering malformed input but covers one of three reachable exception classes.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` marks the response publicly cacheable, but the body varies by `Referer` (the `targetOrigin` interpolation) with **no `Vary: Referer`**. A shared cache/CDN serves referer-A's response to referer-B: resize silently breaks for every publisher behind the cache, and an attacker who primes the cache controls that targetOrigin for later victims.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — Same directive also caches the transient `loading` placeholder for 60s while its own script reloads at 30s — the reload is served from cache, so the visitor sits on "Loading Discussion…" for at least a full minute after the import completes.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26,28 — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is **not a valid XFO directive** (only `DENY`/`SAMEORIGIN`/`ALLOW-FROM`); browsers that don't recognize it treat the header as malformed. No `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors` fallback. Framing protection rests entirely on the spoofable Referer check.

lib/post_creator.rb:216 — New `:cook_method` pass-through is undocumented (absent from the "Acceptable options" block at lines 10-33), unvalidated against `Post.cook_methods`, and applied on `present?`. An out-of-range or typo'd value is silently accepted on the most widely-called constructor in the app, and the value it gates renders raw HTML.

lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `skip_validations` flips `@post.save` to `save(validate: …)` on the **shared** revision path for all post edits, but the return value is still discarded and `revise!` still returns `true` unconditionally. A failed or invalid save is now indistinguishable from a good one, and a misspelled key silently reverts to full validation — exactly the case `TopicEmbed.import` depends on. No post_revisor spec added.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — `feed_key` builds a `feed-modified:<sha1>` redis key that is **never read or written anywhere** — the intended conditional-GET short-circuit was never wired up. Every poll (hourly *and* every on-demand invocation from #7) re-downloads and re-parses the full feed and re-SHA1s every item. Dead code that reads as an implemented feature.

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — No `sidekiq_options`, so the job inherits the 25-retry schedule — but retries are useless by construction: the first retry fires inside the 60s throttle window, `retrieved_recently?` returns true, `retrieve` no-ops, and the job reports **success** without ever refetching. The throttle key is also set before the fetch and never cleared on failure, so a failed attempt is sticky.

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1-24 — New production file with **no spec at all**. Untested: the blank-`embed_url` raise, the user lookup, and `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` — the privilege check deciding whether the rate limit is bypassed. The controller spec's `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` has no `.with(...)`, so nothing asserts a non-staff user gets `no_throttle: false`.

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12-28 — The three "requires X" examples each stub one setting and rely on the other two sitting at falsy defaults — so `poll_feed` would not be called regardless of stubbing. Remove any single guard from `execute` and all three still pass. The `embed_by_username.present?` check (whose removal NPEs on `.downcase`) ships green.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8-11 — Named "is 404 without an embed_url", but with `embeddable_host` unstubbed at `''` the before_filter raises first and the request never reaches `params.require`. Passes identically if `params.require` is deleted; asserts nothing about 404.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:35-38 — Expectations live in an `after` block, obscuring which example failed — and `response.should be_success` is near-vacuous: controller specs don't render views, and in the line-48 example `TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil, so a 200 with `@topic_view = nil` passes undetected. This is the mechanism that lets finding #1 ship green.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:24-27 — `ensure_embeddable` is tested only for blank host and nil referer. **Untested: a referer from a different host** — the actual abuse case — and the new `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` branch. All three negative assertions are `should_not be_success`, which passes on an unintended 500.

spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:39-42 — The update-path test never asserts `content_sha1` was advanced, never asserts no duplicate Topic/TopicEmbed row was created, and there is no example for the unchanged-content case. Break the sha1 comparison so every poll re-revises and this spec passes — that being the single most likely regression in the feature.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `force: true` on a brand-new table converts the loudest failure signal (`PG::DuplicateTable`) into a silent `DROP TABLE`. Losing these rows isn't cosmetic: `topic_id_for_embed` then returns nil for every URL and the next poll re-imports every article as a duplicate topic.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4-5 — `topic_id`/`post_id` are `null: false` with **no index and no foreign key**, and the model's `belongs_to` has no `dependent:`. Root cause of findings #26 and #27; any cleanup query or association join is a sequential scan.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `embed_url` is `:string` (varchar(255)) under a UNIQUE index. Feed/article URLs routinely exceed 255 chars; PG raises rather than truncating, the insert dies inside `Topic.transaction`, and the article is silently dropped from every subsequent poll. Should be `:text`.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << "…"` mutates the caller's String in place across a public class-method boundary. `import_remote` passes `doc.content` straight through, mutating the Readability document as a side effect; any caller that reuses or retries with the same string gets the footer appended repeatedly — and the `content_sha1` on line 16 is computed over the mutated value. A frozen literal raises.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8-13 — The resize message is sent once from `window.onload`, `if (parent)` is always truthy (`parent === window` unframed), and there is no re-send on image/font load or content change and no protocol version field. Height is measured before late-loading avatars settle → clipped or over-tall frames with no recovery path.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — `import_remote` and `import` have **inconsistent failure contracts** on the same class — one raises, one returns nil for a bad URL. Both callers (`topic_retriever.rb:52`, `disqus.thor:148`) handle only the nil case.

config/site_settings.yml:353-357 — The whole new `embedding:` group uses bare scalars with no `enum:`/validator/type hint, despite containing the security boundary (`embeddable_host`) and an outbound-fetch target (`feed_polling_url`). An admin typing `http://example.com/` or `www.example.com` gets a silently non-functional embed, because both consumers do exact `==` against `URI#host`.
app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is dead — nothing here touches `Email::Sender`. Copy-paste from another job.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28`, `topic_embed.rb:45 — Inline `require` inside method bodies while the same file has top-level requires. The gems are `require: false` deliberately, but burying the load in a method body means a missing/broken gem surfaces as a runtime job failure rather than a boot failure.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:21-30` + `poll_feed.rb:31 — One write transaction per feed item, unbounded and serial, inside a `retry: false` job with no batching or item limit. A mid-feed failure leaves the import partially done with no resume point.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 — `if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` compares both default ports regardless of scheme instead of `uri.default_port`, so `https://host:80/x` loses its explicit port. Related gap at lines 64/70: only `/`-prefixed URLs are absolutized, so document-relative (`images/x.jpg`) stays broken and protocol-relative (`//cdn/x.jpg`) is **corrupted** into `http://host//cdn/x.jpg`.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 — `comments.appendChild(iframe)` with no null check on `getElementById('discourse-comments')`. A `<script>` in `<head>` (the common case) throws a TypeError that aborts the IIFE, so the `message` listener at line 25 is never registered either.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — `discourseUrl + "embed/best?…"` assumes a trailing slash, with no normalization and no documented contract for the two globals. Every embedder hand-writes these; a missing slash yields a silently broken path. The new route is also unversioned with no format constraint.
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:21 — `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"` sets the HTML content attribute, which takes a bare number, not a CSS length — relies on browser error-recovery.

lib/post_creator.rb:216 — `cook_method` pass-through has no trusted-caller guard. If any request path ever reaches `PostCreator` with a params-derived `cook_method`, ordinary users post unsanitized HTML. Hardening flag — `PostsController` not present in this checkout to confirm the params whitelist.

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:10 — `raise Discourse::InvalidParameters` for a permanently-invalid argument sends the job through the full ~21-day retry schedule before the dead set. Non-retryable errors should be logged and discarded.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:62-73 — `absolutize_urls` duplicates the rewrite loop twice, differing only in selector/attribute (the img block even keeps the block variable named `a`). A fix for protocol-relative URLs (#54) will land in one and not the other.

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Backfill uses literal `1` rather than `Post.cook_methods[:regular]`; correctness depends on the `Enum` being 1-based, an invariant asserted nowhere in the diff. If it ever changes, the whole `posts` table is mislabelled and `Post#cook` starts returning raw HTML for ordinary posts.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — `TopicView.new(topic_id, …)` with no rescue and no check that the topic still exists or is visible anonymously. Separately, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` immediately returns if a `TopicEmbed` exists for the URL (`return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`), so if a stale `TopicEmbed` row remains after a topic is deleted/hidden, the embed cannot self-heal by refetching. Whether it manifests as a 500 or a handled 404 depends on global exception handling/`TopicView` internals not shown here, but the diff does introduce a real stale-reference failure mode with no recovery path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-29 — Check-then-insert race against the new UNIQUE index: `where(embed_url:).first` … HTTP fetch … `create!`. PollFeed (hourly) and RetrieveTopic (per request) interleave, and `no_throttle` for staff removes the guard entirely. Loser hits the unique violation, aborting the transaction and killing the enclosing job; with `retry: false` the rest of that feed run is never processed.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed later (after doing work like `PostCreator#create` inside a transaction) by `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. With the newly added UNIQUE index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, two concurrent callers (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever`, or two requests) can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race to `create!`, causing an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` / unique constraint violation. There is no rescue, so the exception will abort the transaction and fail the enclosing job/loop. Additionally, `Jobs::PollFeed` sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single such failure can terminate that scheduled run without retrying, preventing the remaining feed items from being processed in that run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — `params.require(:embed_url)` accepts arrays and hashes. `?embed_url[]=a&embed_url[]=b` enqueues an Array; `URI(array)` raises `TypeError`/`ArgumentError`, which the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` does **not** catch. adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` does not enforce a scalar; Rails will allow `embed_url` to be an Array/Hash (e.g. `embed_url[]=a&embed_url[]=b`). That value is passed through to `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`. In `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`, the only validation is `args[:embed_url].present?`, so an Array/Hash passes. It then calls `TopicRetriever.new(args[:embed_url], ...)`, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` does `URI(@embed_url).host` rescuing only `URI::InvalidURIError`. Passing a non-String (Array/Hash) can raise `TypeError` (and in some cases `ArgumentError`) which will not be rescued, causing the job to error. Since the job does not set `sidekiq_options retry: false`, Sidekiq will retry by default, so malformed requests can enqueue hard-failing retrying jobs. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` marks the response publicly cacheable, but the body varies by `Referer` (the `targetOrigin` interpolation) with **no `Vary: Referer`**. A shared cache/CDN serves referer-A's response to referer-B: resize silently breaks for every publisher behind the cache, and an attacker who primes the cache controls that targetOrigin for later victims.

The loading template auto-reloads the same URL after 30s (`document.location.reload()`), but if `discourse_expires_in` sets cache headers with a 60s max-age for that response, the reload request within that minute can be served from cache and return the same loading placeholder even after the background job has created the topic. This is a concrete interaction between the cache directive in the controller and the 30s reload in the view, and can delay showing the imported content until the 60s cache expires.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26,28 — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is **not a valid XFO directive** (only `DENY`/`SAMEORIGIN`/`ALLOW-FROM`); browsers that don't recognize it treat the header as malformed. In Rails, `:string` maps to `varchar(255)` by default, so any embed/feed URL longer than 255 characters will fail to insert (PostgreSQL raises an error rather than truncating). Since `TopicEmbed.import` does `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a `Topic.transaction`, such an insert error would abort the transaction and prevent the embed record/topic from being created, causing repeated failures on subsequent polls/retrieval attempts. In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents << "..."` appends to the *same String object* passed in by the caller, which is an observable side effect across a public class-method boundary. This is verifiable from the diff: the mutation happens before `content_sha1` is computed, so callers that reuse the same string object (or retry with it) will get the footer appended repeatedly and a different SHA1 each time. Additionally, if a caller ever passes a frozen string, this line will raise at runtime. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44 — `import_remote` and `import` have **inconsistent failure contracts** on the same class — one raises, one returns nil for a bad URL. Both callers (`topic_retriever.rb:52`, `disqus.thor:148`) handle only the nil case.

Call sites don’t rescue: `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` with no exception handling, and `disqus.thor` only checks `if post.present?` (nil case) after calling `import_remote`. adjudication_records.issue_text: config/site_settings.yml:353-357 — The whole new `embedding:` group uses bare scalars with no `enum:`/validator/type hint, despite containing the security boundary (`embeddable_host`) and an outbound-fetch target (`feed_polling_url`). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:21-30` + `poll_feed.rb:31 — One write transaction per feed item, unbounded and serial, inside a `retry: false` job with no batching or item limit. A mid-feed failure leaves the import partially done with no resume point.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 — `if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` compares both default ports regardless of scheme instead of `uri.default_port`, so `https://host:80/x` loses its explicit port. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 — `comments.appendChild(iframe)` with no null check on `getElementById('discourse-comments')`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — `discourseUrl + "embed/best?…"` assumes a trailing slash, with no normalization and no documented contract for the two globals. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:21 — `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"` sets the HTML content attribute, which takes a bare number, not a CSS length — relies on browser error-recovery.

So this is not a clear, verifiable defect introduced by the diff—at most it’s an unnecessary unit suffix, not a real correctness bug relying on “error recovery.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_creator.rb:216 — `cook_method` pass-through has no trusted-caller guard.
